prerequisites: It is highly recommended that the student has acquired the competencies corresponding to the subjects of previous semesters.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Ability to write, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in competence G01.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan within companies and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Applied knowledge of logistics systems and production management.
Applied knowledge for occupational safety and health and prevention of occupational risks, execution and direction of plans and projects.
Applied knowledge of passive and active fire protection.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to adapt to new situations.
Ability to communicate with non-experts in the field.
Ability for autonomous and deep learning.
Social attitude of ethical and deontological commitment.
Ability to manage information in solving problematic situations.
Ability to interpret technical documentation.
Ability to consider environmental factors in decision-making.
Ability for critical reasoning.
Assertive behavior.
Interpersonal skills.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team.
Be able to apply knowledge about occupational safety and health and prevention of occupational risks, as well as passive and active fire protection.

syllabus_topics: Topic 0. Basic legislation in Occupational Risk Prevention. - Law 31/95 - RD 39/97 - RD 486/97
Topic 1. Introduction to working conditions -Introduction -General concepts about work -Health -Evaluation of working conditions

Topic 2. General risks in Industry and applicable preventive measures. -Falls of people to different levels. -Falls of people to the same level. -Falls of objects due to collapse or demolition. -Falls of objects during handling. -Detached falling objects. -Stepping on objects. -Collisions against immobile objects. -Collisions against mobile objects. -Bumps / cuts by objects or tools. -Projection of fragments or particles. -Entrapment by or between objects. -Entrapment due to overturning of machines or vehicles. -Overexertion. -Exposure to extreme environmental temperatures. -Thermal contacts. -Direct electrical contacts. -Indirect electrical contacts. -Exposure to harmful or toxic substances and contacts with caustic and/or corrosive substances. -Exposure to radiation. -Fire. -Explosions. -Fire fighting means.
Topic 3. Introduction to Work Safety. -Introduction -Preventive techniques. -Occupational Risk Assessment.
Topic 4. Prevention Planning. -Introduction. -Fundamentals. -Prevention Plan. -Documentary simplification for the prevention plan.
Topic 5. Safety inspection. -Safety inspections -Planned work observations -System evaluation and control -Practical cases on safety inspection.
Topic 6. Accident notification, registration and statistics. -Accident statistics in Spain. -Accident notification and registration. -Statistical indices. -INSST help tools.
Topic 7. Work accidents -Introduction -Concept of Work Accidents -Occupational disease -Types of work accidents -Costs of accidents
Topic 8. Accident investigation. -Legal basis. -Investigation methodology. -Elaboration of the cause tree.

Topic 9. Personal Protective Equipment. -Legal basis. -Guide for selection. -Categories of PPE. -Respiratory protective equipment. -Foot and leg protection. -Head protection. -Eye and face protection. -Hearing protection. -Fall protection. -Hand and arm protection. -Protective clothing.

Topic 10. Machine protection -Legal basis. -Adaptation of machines to current legislation. -Design criteria. -Classification of machinery-specific risks. -Safety measures in machines. -Guards, defenses and safety devices.
Topic 11. Standards and signage. -Introduction. -Applicable legislation. -Standards. -General, specific, evacuation and fire safety signage.
Practice 1. Adaptation of a company to current legislation.
Practice 5. Plant layout for a self-protection plan (signage and evacuation).
teaching_methods: Non-contact learning activities (preparation of a practical report)
Evaluation activities (continuous assessment tests, defense of practical work, global exam)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment of practical work (report, presentation, and defense of practical work)
Continuous assessment of theory: final exam (written, potentially oral with written record)
